Definition: from G1410; force (literally or figuratively); specially, miraculous power (usually by implication, a miracle itself):--ability, abundance, meaning, might(-ily, -y, -y deed), (worker of) miracle(-s), power, strength, violence, mighty (wonderful) work.
BiblicalUsage: Power, the power of God unto salvation, the power the disciples would receive when the Holy Ghost came upon them, and the power that makes the preaching of the cross foolishness to the perishing and salvation to the saved. Paul prays that God would do exceeding abundantly above all we ask or think, according to the power that works in us.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the power of God is not a force I summon but a Person who fills me, and the gospel is powerful because Christ is in it. The same power that raised Him from the dead works in me, and it is able to do far more than I ask.
